reinstating (R) a PENDING provider makes it ACTIVE (D-027); notification-service then also sends an APPROVED notice besides the reinstatement notice, which the legacy does not: D-034 (answer A to Q-128)

PRVRSK01 resets the due date of every provider to today + 5 years on every daily run (20311120 here); the modern system sets a due date only at approval or a completed revalidation (D-003), so it leaves the date as it was (or unset) in this run
the legacy stub rows carry no source, no verdict date and no detail; the replaced screening service fills them from its mocked sources (the field contents are the Q-045/C-7 default)
sanction S gives DENIED in the legacy (PRVSAN01.cbl:109-110) and the new SUSPENDED status in the modern system

the legacy name is the first 60 bytes of PRV-VARIANT (an individual: last name, first name and the start of the licence number; an organisation: legal name and the start of the DBA name); the modern name is composed (first + last, or the legal name)
an unknown action code X is rejected by the modern run (no change, no notice); the legacy applies nothing but still queues the general notice PRVNTGEN (D-012: notification-service replaces the CALL)

effective date of a new provider: the legacy keeps the effective date of the intake record (20260115, D-025); provider-service sets the registration date, the date of the modern run (read from its manifest): decision D-031 (answer A to Q-125, 2026-11-24)

the legacy PRVRSK01 sets a tier on every record whatever its status and screen flag; risk-service assigns a tier only after a PASS screening (MAM-35 AC-6), so denied or failed providers keep a blank tier: D-033 (answer A to Q-127)
